f.title: Apply the regulatory definitions of serious ADR and serious unexpected ADR
f.statement: A serious adverse drug reaction is an adverse drug reaction that requires in-patient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization, causes congenital malformation, results in persistent or significant disability or incapacity, is life threatening or results in death. A serious unexpected adverse drug reaction is a serious adverse drug reaction that is not identified in nature, severity or frequency in the risk information set out in the investigator's brochure or on the label of the drug.
f.applicability: Clinical trials in Canada for which a CTA or CTA-A has been filed (Phase I-III, comparative bioavailability, marketed drugs used outside NOC/DIN parameters)

rows.quote: Serious Adverse Drug Reaction: An adverse drug reaction that requires in-patient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization, that causes congenital malformation, that results in persistent or significant disability or incapacity, that is life threatening or that results in death. Serious Unexpected Adverse Drug Reaction: A serious adverse drug reaction that is not identified in nature, severity or frequency in the risk information set out in the investigator’s brochure or on the label of the drug.

f.title: Notify and file a CTA-A within 15 days after an immediate safety amendment
f.statement: CTA-As must be authorized by Health Canada before the changes are implemented. However, if the sponsor is required to make one or more of the amendments referred to in C.05.008(2) immediately because the clinical trial or the use of the drug endangers the health of clinical trial subjects or other persons, the sponsor may make the amendment immediately without prior review by Health Canada. The sponsor must then notify Health Canada of the change, provide the rationale for immediate implementation and file a CTA-A that clearly identifies the change and that rationale, within 15 days after the date the amendment was implemented.
f.applicability: Clinical trials in Canada for which a CTA or CTA-A has been filed (Phase I-III, comparative bioavailability, marketed drugs used outside NOC/DIN parameters)
f.exceptions: Immediate implementation without prior review applies only where the trial or the use of the drug endangers the health of clinical trial subjects or other persons.

rows.deadline: Within 15 days after the date of implementation of the amendment
rows.quote: CTA-As must be authorized by Health Canada prior to implementation of the changes [C.05.008]. However, if the sponsor is required to immediately make one or more of the amendments referred to in subsection (2) of C.05.008 because the clinical trial or the use of the drug for the purposes of the clinical trial endangers the health of clinical trial subjects or other persons, the sponsor may immediately make the amendment without prior review by Health Canada. Sponsors must notify Health Canada of this change, provide the relevant rationale in support of the immediate implementation and file a CTA-A that clearly identifies the change and the rationale for immediate implementation of the change within 15 days after the date of implementation of the amendment [C.05.008(4)].
rows.review_note: Review: added - urgent safety measure route with its 15-day notification/CTA-A clock (clock starts on the date of implementation). Sponsors may only resume the trial when a No Objection Letter has been issued by the appropriate Directorate or the 30-day default period has passed without an objection. Sponsors should also file a completed CTSI form before resuming the trial.

f.exceptions: CTA-Notification route only if there are no changes to the protocol or to Chemistry and Manufacturing.

f.title: Notify study completion or site closure by CTA-Notification
f.statement: The sponsor is requested to notify the relevant Directorate(s), via CTA-Notification, when a clinical trial is completed or a clinical trial site is closed. Notwithstanding a suspension, cancellation or closure of the trial in Canada, a study is considered completed only after the last subject globally completes the 'end of study' visit defined in the protocol, which is the final visit for study-related tests and procedures, including capture of any final potential study-related adverse events.
f.applicability: Clinical trials in Canada for which a CTA or CTA-A has been filed (Phase I-III, comparative bioavailability, marketed drugs used outside NOC/DIN parameters)

rows.quote: The sponsor is requested to notify the relevant Directorate(s) (via CTA-Notification) when a clinical trial is completed or a clinical trial site is closed. Notwithstanding a suspension, cancellation or study closure of a clinical trial in Canada, in its entirety, a study is considered to be completed after the last subject globally completes the "end of study" visit as defined in the protocol. The "end of study visit" is the final visit for study-related tests and procedures, including the capture of any final potential study-related adverse events, and usually occurs some time after the subject has completed/discontinued study drug administration. The "end of study visit" is normally an in-person visit, but for some studies it can also be carried out over the telephone.
rows.review_note: Review: added - completion notification ('is requested', so Recommended) with the global end-of-study definition that sets how long Division 5 safety reporting runs (see 0007). f.title: Continue Division 5 safety monitoring and reporting while a study remains ongoing beyond treatment
f.statement: Where a study is considered ongoing well beyond the period of study treatment (for example gene therapies or drugs with very long half-lives of several months), long-term safety monitoring and reporting would be required in accordance with Part C, Division 5 of the Regulations for as long as the study is ongoing. The reporting requirements for such long-term safety follow-up are normally specified in the study protocol and agreed between the sponsor and Health Canada before the clinical trial is authorized in Canada.
f.legal_basis: Food and Drug Regulations Part C, Division 5
f.applicability: Studies considered ongoing beyond study treatment (e.g., gene therapies, drugs with very long half-lives)

rows.quote: It should be noted, however, that there may be certain scenarios [e.g., gene therapies, drugs with very long half-lives (i.e., several months)] where a study may be considered to be ongoing well beyond the period of study treatment, i.e., where long-term safety monitoring and reporting would be required in accordance with Division 5. The reporting requirements with regards to such long-term follow-up of safety are normally specified in the study protocol and agreed to between the sponsor and Health Canada prior to the authorization of the clinical trial in Canada.
rows.review_note: Review: extractor flag decided - kept Mandatory. Double-check: confirmed the statement stays within the quote. Below 90: judgement call - 'would be required in accordance with Division 5' restates existing Division 5 duties conditionally rather than creating one; Mandatory/Regulation is the reviewer's reading of a guidance sentence; the trigger (study considered ongoing) is case-specific.

f.title: Do not expedite reactions judged unrelated by both investigator and sponsor
f.statement: Adverse reactions that are considered unrelated to the study drug by both the investigator and the sponsor should not be reported (in the context of the expedited reporting criteria of 2.8.4.2).
f.clause: 2.8.4.2 Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs) Reporting Criteria (3) Causality
f.applicability: Clinical trials in Canada for which a CTA or CTA-A has been filed (Phase I-III, comparative bioavailability, marketed drugs used outside NOC/DIN parameters)

rows.quote: Concomitantly, adverse reactions that are considered to be unrelated to the study drug by both the investigator and the sponsor should not be reported.

Below 90: the 'in the context of the expedited reporting criteria' tie in the statement is inferred from the section, not the sentence; passive, actor inferred.

f.title: Attach Form 01-03 and the CIOMS form to ADR reports sent to Health Canada
f.statement: When submitting an ADR report to Health Canada, a complete ADR Expedited Reporting Summary Form (Form 01-03) and the CIOMS Form should be attached and, as applicable, mailed or faxed to the Biologics and Genetic Therapies Directorate (biologics and radiopharmaceuticals) or the Therapeutic Products Directorate (pharmaceuticals).
f.applicability: Clinical trials in Canada for which a CTA or CTA-A has been filed (Phase I-III, comparative bioavailability, marketed drugs used outside NOC/DIN parameters)

rows.quote: When submitting an ADR report to Health Canada, a complete ADR Expedited Reporting Summary Form (Form 01-03) and the CIOMS Form should be attached and as applicable be mailed or faxed to:
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed against the quote. Below 90: passive wording, so the sponsor actor is inferred from context; the destination directorates come from an address table after the quote.

f.title: Provide C.05.012 records or safety information when Health Canada requests them during the trial
f.statement: Health Canada may request a sponsor, at any time during an ongoing clinical trial, to submit information or records kept under C.05.012 in order to assess the safety of the drug; the safety report could include a line listing of all serious events and/or other expected and unexpected ADRs.
f.applicability: Clinical trials in Canada for which a CTA or CTA-A has been filed (Phase I-III, comparative bioavailability, marketed drugs used outside NOC/DIN parameters)

rows.quote: Health Canada may request a sponsor, at any time during an ongoing clinical trial, to submit information or records kept under C.05.012 in order to assess the safety of the drug. Double-check: confirmed against the quote. Below 90: authority-only row (Health Canada may request); the sponsor's response is not worded as a separate duty here.

f.title: Identify in the protocol serious events treated as disease-related and exempt from expedited reporting
f.statement: When a fatal or other serious outcome is the primary efficacy endpoint in a clinical trial, the protocol should clearly indicate the serious event(s) that will be treated as disease-related and not subject to expedited reporting.
f.applicability: Trials where a fatal or other serious outcome is the primary efficacy endpoint

rows.quote: When a fatal or other serious outcome is the primary efficacy endpoint in a clinical trial, the protocol should clearly indicate the serious event(s) that will be treated as disease-related and not subject to expedited reporting.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed against the quote. Below 90: passive wording, so the sponsor actor is inferred from context ('the protocol should clearly indicate').

f.title: Rapidly communicate other information that may influence risk-benefit or trial conduct, such as increased rates of expected serious ADRs
f.statement: Situations beyond individual SUADR reports may necessitate rapid communication to Health Canada, and appropriate scientific and medical judgment should be applied to each situation; examples are information that might influence the risk-benefit assessment of a drug, or that would be sufficient to consider changes in drug administration or in the overall conduct of a clinical trial, including a clinically important increase in the rate of occurrence of an expected serious ADR.
f.applicability: Clinical trials in Canada for which a CTA or CTA-A has been filed (Phase I-III, comparative bioavailability, marketed drugs used outside NOC/DIN parameters)

rows.quote: There are situations in addition to the above that may necessitate rapid communication to Health Canada, and appropriate scientific and medical judgment should be applied to each situation. For example, information that might influence the risk-benefit assessment of a drug, or that would be sufficient to consider changes in drug administration, or in the overall conduct of a clinical trial, represent such situations; including: a) For an “expected” serious ADR, an increase in the rate of occurrence which is judged clinically important;
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed against the quote. Below 90: judgement-based 'may necessitate rapid communication' with examples; no actor named; list continues in 0018.

f.title: Submit significant hazards and major animal safety findings to the relevant Directorate
f.statement: Other situations that may necessitate rapid communication include a significant hazard to the patient population, such as lack of efficacy with a drug used in treating a life-threatening disease, and a major safety finding from a newly completed animal study; this information should be submitted, where applicable, to the Biologics and Genetic Therapies Directorate or the Office of Clinical Trials, Therapeutic Products Directorate.
f.applicability: Clinical trials in Canada for which a CTA or CTA-A has been filed (Phase I-III, comparative bioavailability, marketed drugs used outside NOC/DIN parameters)

rows.quote: b) A significant hazard to the patient population, such as lack of efficacy with a drug used in treating a life-threatening disease; and c) A major safety finding from a newly completed animal study. This information should be submitted where applicable to either:

f.title: Follow ICH E6 and E2A for safety reporting to qualified investigators and REBs
f.statement: Sponsors should refer to ICH Guidance Documents E6 (Good Clinical Practice) and E2A (Clinical Safety Data Management) for safety reporting requirements to qualified investigator(s) and their Research Ethics Board(s).
f.applicability: Clinical trials in Canada for which a CTA or CTA-A has been filed (Phase I-III, comparative bioavailability, marketed drugs used outside NOC/DIN parameters)

rows.quote: Sponsors should refer to ICH Guidance Documents E6: Guideline for Good Clinical Practice and E2A: Clinical Safety Data Management for safety reporting requirements to Qualified Investigator(s) and their Research Ethics Board(s).

f.title: Review the Investigator's Brochure, including safety information, at least annually
f.statement: In accordance with ICH GCP, the IB, including all safety information and global status, should be reviewed at least annually and revised as necessary; more frequent revision may be appropriate depending on the stage of development and the generation of relevant new information.
f.applicability: Clinical trials in Canada for which a CTA or CTA-A has been filed (Phase I-III, comparative bioavailability, marketed drugs used outside NOC/DIN parameters)

f.title: File the updated IB with the next CTA/CTA-A/CTA-N or separately as a CTA-N with a protocol/ICF statement
f.statement: If the sponsor is planning to submit a CTA, or planning or required to submit a CTA-A or CTA-N, the updated IB should be submitted with that application; otherwise the updated IB should be submitted separately as a CTA-N and include a statement confirming that the protocol and/or ICF of all ongoing trials do not require changes as a result of the updated IB.
f.applicability: Clinical trials in Canada for which a CTA or CTA-A has been filed (Phase I-III, comparative bioavailability, marketed drugs used outside NOC/DIN parameters)

f.title: Accompany every updated IB with a list of changes and the rationale for each
f.statement: In all cases, the updated IB should be accompanied by a list of changes that clearly describes the sections that have changed, including a rationale for each change.
f.applicability: Clinical trials in Canada for which a CTA or CTA-A has been filed (Phase I-III, comparative bioavailability, marketed drugs used outside NOC/DIN parameters)

f.title: Record, handle and store all clinical trial information to allow complete and accurate reporting, interpretation and verification
f.statement: The sponsor shall record, handle and store all information in respect of a clinical trial in a way that allows its complete and accurate reporting as well as its interpretation and verification.
f.clause: 2.8.6 Records related to CTAs and CTA-As (a)
f.applicability: Clinical trials in Canada for which a CTA or CTA-A has been filed (Phase I-III, comparative bioavailability, marketed drugs used outside NOC/DIN parameters)
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Clinical safety monitoring

f.title: Maintain complete and accurate records establishing GCP and regulatory compliance of the trial
f.statement: The sponsor shall maintain complete and accurate records to establish that the clinical trial is conducted in accordance with good clinical practices and the Regulations.
f.clause: 2.8.6 Records related to CTAs and CTA-As (b)
f.applicability: Clinical trials in Canada for which a CTA or CTA-A has been filed (Phase I-III, comparative bioavailability, marketed drugs used outside NOC/DIN parameters)

f.title: Keep all IB versions and records of each IB change with rationale and supporting documentation
f.statement: The sponsor shall maintain complete and accurate records in respect of the use of a drug in a clinical trial, including a copy of all versions of the IB for the drug and records respecting each change made to the IB, including the rationale for each change and documentation that supports each change.
f.clause: 2.8.6 Records related to CTAs and CTA-As (c)(i)-(ii)
f.applicability: Clinical trials in Canada for which a CTA or CTA-A has been filed (Phase I-III, comparative bioavailability, marketed drugs used outside NOC/DIN parameters)

f.title: Keep records of all adverse events, inside or outside Canada, with indication and dosage form
f.statement: Among the records the sponsor shall maintain (C.05.012(c)): records respecting all adverse events in respect of the drug that have occurred inside or outside Canada, including information that specifies the indication for use and the dosage form of the drug at the time of the adverse event.

f.title: Keep enrolment records that allow every trial subject to be identified and contacted
f.statement: Among the records the sponsor shall maintain (C.05.012(c)): records respecting the enrolment of clinical trial subjects, including information sufficient to enable all clinical trial subjects to be identified and contacted in the event that the sale of the drug may endanger the health of the clinical trial subjects or other persons.

f.title: Keep records of shipment, receipt, disposition, return and destruction of the trial drug
f.statement: Among the records the sponsor shall maintain (C.05.012(c)): records respecting the shipment, receipt, disposition, return and destruction of the drug.
f.clause: 2.8.6 Records related to CTAs and CTA-As (c)(v)

f.title: Keep a signed QI undertaking for each site covering GCP and informing subjects and REB of discontinuation risks
f.statement: Among the records the sponsor shall maintain (C.05.012(c)): for each clinical trial site, an undertaking signed and dated by the qualified investigator before commencing their responsibilities, stating that the QI will conduct the trial in accordance with GCP and will immediately, on discontinuance of the trial by the sponsor (in its entirety or at a site), inform both the subjects and the REB of the discontinuance, provide the reasons and advise them in writing of any potential risks to the health of subjects or other persons.
f.clause: 2.8.6 Records related to CTAs and CTA-As (c)(vi)

rows.quote: vi) for each clinical trial site, an undertaking from the qualified investigator that is signed and dated by the qualified investigator prior to the commencement of his or her responsibilities in respect of the clinical trial, that states that:  the qualified investigator will conduct the clinical trial in accordance with GCPs, and  the qualified investigator will immediately, on discontinuance of the clinical trial by the sponsor, in its entirety or at a clinical trial site, inform both the clinical trial subjects and the REB of the discontinuance, provide them with the reasons for the discontinuance and advise them in writing of any potential risks to the health of clinical trial subjects or other persons;

f.statement: Among the records the sponsor shall maintain (C.05.012(c)): for each clinical trial site, a copy of the protocol, ICF and any amendment to them approved by the REB for that site; and an attestation, signed and dated by the REB for that site, stating that it has reviewed and approved the protocol and ICF and that the board carries out its functions in a manner consistent with GCPs.

f.title: Provide records within 2 days of a request when there is a concern about risk to trial subjects
f.statement: Records must be made available to the relevant Directorate within 2 days of a request if there is a concern regarding the use of the drug for the purposes of a clinical trial and a risk to the health of the subjects involved in that trial.
f.clause: 2.8.6 Records related to CTAs and CTA-As (C.05.013)

f.title: Provide records within 7 days of any other request
f.statement: In any case other than a concern regarding the use of the drug in the trial and a risk to subjects' health, records must be provided within 7 days of a request.
